LeBron James (born December 30, 1984) is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes ever. He played high school ball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, where he was named USA Today’s National Player of the Year three times.

**NBA career**

* **Miami Heat (2003–2010)** – Drafted first overall in 2003; won two NBA championships (2006, 2012), earned four MVP awards, and became known for his combination of size, speed, strength, and court vision.
* **Cleveland Cavaliers (2010–2014 & 2018–present)** – Returned home to lead Cleveland to its first-ever championship in 2016, earning Finals MVP honors.
* **Los Angeles Lakers (2019–present)** – Joined the Lakers in 2019, winning another title in 2020 during the NBA Bubble season.

**Career highlights**

| Category | Achievements |
|----------|--------------|
| **MVP Awards** | 5× regular-season MVP (2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013) |
| **All-Star Appearances** | 19× All‑Star (since 2005) |
| **Championships** | 4× NBA champion (2006, 2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) |
| **Scoring** | Career average ~27 points per game; multiple seasons averaging over 28 ppg |
| **Versatility** | Known for playing all five positions effectively |

Beyond the hardwood, LeBron has become a prominent philanthropist—most notably through his *I Promise School*, a public charter elementary school in Akron—and a media mogul via Uninterrupted, a streaming platform focused on Black voices. He's also been active in social justice causes, using his platform to speak out against racial inequality and police brutality.

In short, LeBron James is not only a dominant force on the basketball court but also a significant cultural figure whose influence extends far beyond sports.
